model_response: Before Massachusetts passed these resolutions, American troops were already deep inside Mexico. The war ended in 1848 with the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo, which handed the United States the Mexican Cession for $15 million (OI) — which shows the legislature was right that the war was being waged “for the conquest of a portion of her territory.”

source_document: Document 10 — Massachusetts legislature, resolutions on the war with Mexico, April 26, 1847
source_text: Resolved, That the present war with Mexico had its primary origin in the unconstitutional annexation to the United States of the foreign State of Texas; that it was unconstitutionally commenced by the order of the President, to General Taylor, to take military possession of territory in dispute between the United States and Mexico, and in the occupation of Mexico; and that it is now waged by a powerful nation against a weak neighbor—unnecessarily and without just cause, at immense cost of treasure [money] and life, for the dismemberment [carving up] of Mexico, and for the conquest of a portion of her territory, from which slavery has already been excluded, with the triple object of extending slavery, of strengthening the slave power [slaveholders' power in government], and of obtaining the control of the Free States, under the Constitution of the United States.
